business_problem: TVer needed to bring its ad server in-house so it could iterate faster on formats and features while sustaining high availability, millisecond latency, and massive spikes in ad-request traffic without cross-cloud data-transfer costs.
solution_summary: TVer rebuilt its advertising delivery backbone directly on Google Cloud so its ad-serving stack could sit beside the company's BigQuery data platform instead of sending hundreds of millions of daily logs across clouds. The new architecture runs the ad delivery API on GKE Standard and uses a split database design: Memorystore for Redis Cluster is used where strict consistency and ultra-fast responses matter, while Cloud Bigtable handles workloads that prioritize storage scale and cost efficiency. Cloud Logging supports operations, and the team partnered with Google Cloud Consulting (PSO) to review infrastructure, algorithms, and data structures before launch. By colocating compute, storage, and analytics on one platform, TVer completed a zero-downtime migration and created a scalable ad platform for one of Japan's largest streaming services.

solution_components.role: Stores latency-sensitive data where consistency and ultra-fast responses are critical.

solution_components.name: Cloud Bigtable
solution_components.role: Handles large-scale ad-serving data where storage capacity and cost efficiency are prioritized.

data_flow: Viewer ad requests hit the ad delivery API on GKE Standard, which looks up low-latency or high-scale data in Memorystore for Redis Cluster and Cloud Bigtable, then writes and analyzes ad logs in BigQuery while Cloud Logging tracks operations across the platform.
business_outcome: TVer now operates an in-house ad platform on Google Cloud that supports 650 million monthly video views, processes hundreds of millions of daily ad requests with millisecond latency, and eliminated cross-cloud outbound data costs through a zero-downtime migration.

The design intentionally colocates the ad servers with BigQuery to avoid cross-cloud outbound log transfer.
GKE Standard was chosen so capacity could be secured in advance for real-time delivery peaks.
The team plans to keep strengthening the stack with continuous materialized views and Valkey migration.
